title: Do Universities Consider IB Component Scores?
summary: Learn whether universities see IB paper and IA component scores, what appears on official transcripts, and when detailed marks may still affect admission.
body_markdown:
For most IB applications, **universities consider final subject grades rather than the marks from individual assessment components** . The standard IB transcript reports each course and its final grade from **1 to 7** , alongside broader Diploma Programme results. It does not ordinarily provide a paper-by-paper or Internal Assessment mark breakdown.


Component scores still matter because they are weighted and combined to produce each subject grade. They can also become relevant after results if you narrowly miss an offer, investigate an **Enquiry Upon Results (EUR)** , or are specifically asked by a university for additional evidence. This article explains what universities normally receive, what admissions conditions actually measure, and how to respond when detailed marks could help your case.


### What counts as an IB component score?


An IB subject is usually assessed through several components. Depending on the course, these may include written examination papers, an **Internal Assessment (IA)** , an individual oral, an investigation, an exhibition, a performance, or other coursework.


Each component receives a mark and has a specified weighting. The weighted marks are aggregated into a **scaled total mark** , which is then compared with the subject's grade boundaries to produce a final grade from **1 to 7** .


Type of result Example Normally central to admission?


Component mark Paper 1 mark or IA mark No


Scaled total mark Weighted total across the subject Usually no


Subject grade Biology HL grade 6 Yes


HL profile 6, 6, 5 at Higher Level Often


Diploma total 37 points including core points Often


Core outcome TOK and EE grades, plus core points Sometimes


Diploma status Diploma awarded or not awarded Sometimes required


A component mark should not be confused with a **Diploma component** . Universities and UCAS may use “components” to refer broadly to individual IB subjects, Theory of Knowledge, or the Extended Essay. That does not mean they receive every examination-paper mark.


### What universities normally see on an official IB transcript


The IB describes its transcript as an official copy of a candidate's results sent directly to a higher education institution. According to the IB's guide for universities, a Diploma Programme transcript records the student's courses, language of instruction, and final score for each course. For full Diploma candidates, it also records the total points, core information, and Extended Essay subject area.


The standard transcript therefore focuses on **reported outcomes** , not the underlying marking detail. A university would normally see information such as:


- English A: Language and Literature HL -- **6**
- Economics HL -- **7**
- Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL -- **6**
- Total Diploma score -- **39**
- TOK and Extended Essay outcomes
- Whether the Diploma was awarded


It would not normally see that the student earned one percentage on Paper 1, another on Paper 2, and a separate raw IA mark. The IB's current[assessment FAQ](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/assessment-and-exams/getting-results/assessment-faq/) also states that component marks and grades are not shown through the ordinary candidate results view, although a coordinator may give candidates access to additional result details.


Universities can receive authorized IB results electronically through secure systems or as paper transcripts. Students should arrange this through their coordinator before results are released or use the IB's later transcript-request service when necessary. In the UK, UCAS can receive IB results and pass the relevant qualification and subject outcomes to universities when properly authorized.


### What admissions officers actually evaluate


Universities set their own admissions policies, so there is no universal formula. Nevertheless, published IB entry requirements overwhelmingly use **Diploma totals, Higher Level grades, and grades in required subjects** , rather than individual paper or IA scores.


For example, Oxford's published requirement for Medicine is **39 points including core points, with 766 at Higher Level** , alongside required HL subjects. Cambridge's Natural Sciences course similarly publishes a Diploma total and an HL grade profile. These requirements show the level at which admissions decisions are normally expressed.


A typical conditional offer might require:


- **36 points overall**
- **6, 6, 5 at Higher Level**
- **Grade 6 in Mathematics AA HL**
- successful award of the IB Diploma


If a student earns the required Mathematics grade, the university normally does not distinguish between someone whose strongest component was the IA and someone whose strongest component was Paper 2. Both students have demonstrated the final standard represented by the same IB subject grade.


Admissions review may still consider more than final IB results. Depending on the country and institution, universities may assess school transcripts, predicted grades, course difficulty, personal statements, references, admissions tests, interviews, portfolios, contextual information, and relevant extracurricular evidence. These are separate from the official IB component-score breakdown.


### Why component marks still matter


### They determine the final subject grade


Component marks matter most **inside the IB grading process** . A strong IA can compensate partly for a weaker examination, while a weak component can pull down the weighted total. The resulting subject grade is the outcome universities normally use.


Students can model this relationship with the[RevisionDojo IB Grade Calculator](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grade-calculator) . Calculations based on practice results remain estimates because final boundaries, moderation, and official marking determine the actual result.


### They help explain a near miss


Suppose an offer requires a 6 in Chemistry HL, but the student receives a 5 and is one scaled mark below the grade boundary. The university's formal decision still concerns the grade 5, not a particularly strong IA or Paper 2 result. However, boundary proximity may support a prompt, factual conversation with the admissions office while the school considers post-results options.


A university is not obliged to accept a near miss. Some institutions may exercise discretion when places remain available, while highly constrained courses may apply the condition strictly. The practical approach in[RevisionDojo's guide to conditional IB offers](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-university-offer-depends-on-results) is to communicate quickly, identify the exact missed condition, and avoid assuming that a remark will succeed.


### They inform an Enquiry Upon Results decision


Detailed results are particularly useful when deciding whether to request an **Enquiry Upon Results** , commonly called a remark. The candidate-facing information may include the scaled total, grade boundaries, and marks needed for an increase, while the coordinator can advise on component information and eligible services.


A remark can leave a result unchanged and may increase or decrease it where the applicable service allows. It should therefore be based on boundary proximity and a meaningful consequence, such as meeting an offer, rather than disappointment alone. The[RevisionDojo explanation of IB remarks](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-remark-explained) provides a useful decision framework, but the coordinator remains the appropriate source for current deadlines, fees, consent requirements, and available categories.


### Situations in which a university may request more detail


Although component marks are not part of routine transcript-based review, an institution can ask for additional documentation under its own policy. Possible circumstances include:


- verifying an unusual or incomplete qualification record
- reviewing a narrowly missed conditional offer
- determining placement where ordinary documentation is insufficient
- investigating an administrative discrepancy
- assessing an applicant through a country-specific process


A student might also choose to mention a component achievement in an application, but it should be relevant and verifiable. For example, discussing the research skills developed through an IA may strengthen an explanation of academic interest. Claiming that a high IA mark should override the final subject grade is much less persuasive because the university's published requirement normally concerns the official grade.


Scholarships and transfer credit can follow separate rules from admission. UBC, for example, publishes first-year credit thresholds based on final IB course grades. This again illustrates that universities usually recognize the completed course outcome rather than the underlying paper marks, although students must always check the current policy for their institution and programme.


### Predicted grades and school component results


Before final results exist, universities may make decisions using **predicted grades** and the school record. Teachers can consider tests, mock examinations, coursework, IA progress, and observed performance when forming predictions, but universities generally receive the prediction as a subject grade rather than the teacher's complete calculation.


This distinction matters. A university may see a school transcript containing test or semester grades, especially in admissions systems that request a multi-year academic record. Those school-issued marks are not the same as official IB component results.


Students trying to improve their evidence before predictions are finalized should focus on repeated, assessment-aligned performance.[Targeted IB Questionbank practice](https://www.revisiondojo.com/) and timed Mock Exams can expose whether the problem lies in knowledge, command terms, structure, or timing. Jojo AI can help clarify specific errors, but teacher feedback and the official subject criteria should guide judgments about assessed work.


For a clearer account of how evidence can inform a prediction, see RevisionDojo's guide to[how IB predicted grades are calculated](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-are-ib-predicted-grades-calculated) . A prediction is still an estimate, not an unofficial final result.


### What to do before and after IB results


Before results day, read the exact wording of every offer. Record separately the required total, HL profile, subject prerequisites, core conditions, and Diploma-status requirement.


After results are released:


1. **Check the official outcomes.** Confirm your Diploma status, total points, subject grades, and core result.
2. **Compare them with the offer literally.** Do not substitute a strong component mark for a required subject grade.
3. **Ask your coordinator for detail if needed.** Boundary proximity and component information are useful when considering post-results services.
4. **Contact admissions if a condition was missed.** Give your applicant number, achieved result, and any confirmed next step concisely.
5. **Verify transcript delivery.** Universities cannot act on results they have not received.


The IB permits candidates to nominate institutions to receive official results, subject to its current request procedures. The[IB transcript-request page](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/assessment-and-exams/requesting-transcripts/) explains how requests before and after results release are handled.


### Common mistakes to avoid


- **Assuming universities automatically see every mark.** Standard IB reporting emphasizes final course grades and Diploma outcomes.
- **Confusing a scaled total with a component mark.** The scaled total combines weighted components; it is not a Paper 1 or IA score.
- **Treating a near boundary as a higher grade.** Until an official change is issued, the recorded grade remains valid.
- **Sending unsolicited screenshots as proof.** Use the institution's stated document procedure and official transcripts where required.
- **Ignoring subject-specific conditions.** A high total cannot necessarily compensate for missing a required HL grade.
- **Requesting a remark without checking the numbers.** Read the[IB results-day guidance](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-results-day-faq-answering-every-student-question) and consult your coordinator before acting.


### Conclusion


Universities normally consider **final IB subject grades, the HL profile, overall Diploma points, core outcomes, and Diploma status** , not individual exam-paper or IA marks. Component scores matter because they create those final grades and can guide post-results decisions, especially when a conditional offer has been narrowly missed.


Always follow the published policy of the university and course concerned, since institutions can request additional evidence. RevisionDojo's Grade Calculator, Questionbank, Mock Exams, and Jojo AI can help you understand how component performance contributes to your likely overall result, while your IB coordinator should handle official result details and post-results procedures.
